column1: # One row per mixing run you want run_pipeline.R (RUN_ANALYSIS$phreeqc_mixing = TRUE) to execute automatically. sample_ids are real Samples.sample_id values -- never guessed. Set enabled=TRUE to activate a row; leave FALSE/blank to keep it defined but skipped.

column6: 2026-09-12 (session 29): first REAL (non-synthetic) mixing run. Thermal end-member = sample 816 (SBF_0001 fumarole, real 2024-2026 FIELD chemistry, Cl=815 mg/L). Meteoric end-member = sample 829 (Boyd Domestic Well, Cl=45 mg/L). These two samples are NOT collected on the same date -- this is a typical/representative end-member estimate (the same approach Sorey & Colvard's own 820/6 mg/L split uses), not a real-time-paired validation. Computes conservative mixing fractions for all 754 PHREEQC-eligible samples against this pair.

2026-10-25: restructured LST flowpath model per user direction -- fissure (816, SBF_0001) and resort well (815, SBW_0002) are the real upgradient thermal sources (their gas-informed parent-fluid reconstructions agree within ~2% Cl, session 2026-10-24); the real downgradient targets are SBW_0001 (821, across-creek well) and the three real Lower Sinter Terrace springs SBS_0001/0002/0003 (825/820/822) -- NOT hot spring 6 or GS-5, both confirmed (database label + White 1964 text: 'drill holes on the Main Terrace') to be Main Terrace features, not Low Terrace. Meteoric end-member changed from Boyd Domestic Well (829, Cl=45 -- but Ca/Mg far too low vs. regional norms, and sits essentially due north of the fissure at the identical longitude, NOT southwest/west of Steamboat as true upgradient recharge should be) to Jumbo Grade Spring (920, Mariner & Janik 1995 Table 1, Cl=7, real measured pH=8/T=15C) -- chosen on Ca/Mg/alkalinity residual fit (best of 4 candidates tested), but its own coordinates are NOT on file in this database either, so its southwest/west position relative to Steamboat is a plausible-but-UNCONFIRMED assumption, not verified. No geolocated southwest/west regional groundwater sample currently exists in this project. Thermal end-member kept as raw sample 816 (not the gas-informed reconstructed parent fluid itself, which has no sample_id and cannot be fed through compute_mixing_fractions()'s sample_id-based lookup) -- a known simplification, flagged here.

2026-10-25 (correction): meteoric/dilution end-member changed again, from Jumbo Grade Spring (session 2026-10-25, real chemistry fit but NO coordinate on file -- 'a random spring we don't know', per direct user correction) to SBRR (sample 819, Steamboat Creek @ Rhodes Road, upstream-control conductivity-logger/USGS-gauge site) -- a real, precisely located, already-well-characterized site, not a spatial guess. Caveat: SBRR itself is not a pure meteoric water -- it already carries a modest real thermal signature (Cl=17.1 mg/L, temperature=59.36C field-measured, well above a true cold background stream), consistent with sitting close to/downstream of the thermal field itself. Using it as the dilution end-member is therefore a conservative (not a theoretically 'pure') choice, explicitly flagged wherever this run is used, not silently treated as equivalent to a true regional meteoric sample.
